html:
The Temple of Hephaestus is a Doric temple on a low hill above the Agora, the market square of Athens. It was begun in 449 BCE and finished around 415 BCE, and it is one of the best preserved Greek temples anywhere.

It honoured Hephaestus, god of fire and metalwork, together with Athena as goddess of crafts. The streets around it were full of the workshops of potters and bronze smiths. It has six columns across the front and thirteen down each side, and was built in the same years as the Parthenon, the Propylaea and the Erechtheion on the Acropolis. Some scholars think the same architect designed the Temple of Poseidon at Sounion.

For centuries people wrongly called it the Theseion, believing it held the bones of the hero Theseus. From the 7th century it served as the church of Saint George, which is why its roof and columns survived. It was last used for worship in 1834, when King Otto of the new Greece arrived in Athens.
sum: The Temple of Hephaestus is a Doric temple on a low hill above the Agora, the market square of Athens. It was begun in 449 BCE and finished around 415 BCE, and it is one of the best preserved Greek temples anywhere.
